title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

reading.body:
This is an impersonation failure. AI-generated video was used to depict a real candidate saying things she never said, and the output was published to a social media account belonging to her electoral opponent. The harm sits at the point of publication, not at the point of generation: the videos were presented to an audience as if they were real statements by a named person.

Nothing in the deployment appears to have required a human check before posting, and no platform or campaign process is reported to have caught the fakes before they circulated. Catching this would have required either a disclosure that the videos were synthetic or a verification step before they were shared from the account.

What is not established is whether the videos violate state defamation law, whether Van Orden or his campaign intended to deceive anyone, and whether any legal action will follow. A cease-and-desist letter is a demand, not a ruling, and the campaign's response is a statement, not a finding.

reports.title: Cooke campaign sends cease-and-desist to Congressman Van Orden over AI deepfakes

summary:
Attorneys for Democratic congressional candidate Rebecca Cooke sent a cease-and-desist letter to U.S. Rep. Derrick Van Orden, a Republican from Prairie du Chien, over AI-generated videos posted to his X account. The videos show fake versions of Cooke saying things she never said, including a clip shared on Aug. 4. Cooke is challenging Van Orden in November for Wisconsin's 3rd Congressional District.

The letter, dated Sept. 30, says the videos are fiction and could violate state defamation law. Cooke's attorneys say they are monitoring Van Orden's accounts and weighing all legal options if he continues. Van Orden's campaign dismissed the letter as a tantrum, and he responded with another AI video. Cooke lost to Van Orden in 2024 by about 3 percentage points.
